title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act is intended to build and nurture a skilled workforce capable of advancing AI technologies. It proposes increased investment in education, training, and research to support the growth of a robust AI talent pipeline and foster innovation.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill proposes that AI systems be required to have detailed functional bills of materials, clearly documenting the components, data, and processes used in their development and deployment. It also includes additional provisions for overseeing AI usage and governance.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act is a proposed law that aims to clarify how artificial intelligence tools can be used in schools, ensuring teachers, students, and administrators understand their purpose and limitations. It establishes guidelines for responsible AI deployment, promotes transparency about data use, and sets standards to protect student privacy while encouraging the educational benefits of AI technologies.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for teaching artificial intelligence skills from elementary to high school. It allocates funding, offers teacher training, and supplies educational resources to help students and educators prepare for an AI‑driven future.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes regulations to ensure that AI-powered toys designed for children are safe and secure. The law requires manufacturers to meet strict safety standards, disclose AI functions, and protect children’s personal data.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says that anyone in the United States who is affected by building or running an artificial intelligence data center has a right to know what is happening and to have a say in the process. The goal is to give communities local control and ensure decisions are made transparently.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act prohibits the creation of AI data centers on federal property. It seeks to protect national land resources and prevent the expansion of large AI infrastructure onto federal lands.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 creates a framework to guide the use of AI in programs serving U.S. veterans, emphasizing safety, fairness, and transparency. It establishes a regulatory body that will monitor AI deployments, enforce compliance, and protect veterans’ privacy and well‑being.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The AI Act of 2026 is designed to prevent the creation and use of artificial intelligence systems that generate or spread false or misleading information that could be used to exploit individuals or groups. It sets out rules, oversight, and penalties for developers and users to ensure AI is employed responsibly and transparently.

title: A bill to require a report on the artificial intelligence power of the People's Republic of China.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: This bill mandates a comprehensive report on China’s artificial intelligence capabilities. The report is intended to assess the country’s AI power and inform U.S. policy decisions.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for studying how artificial intelligence tools are used within the judicial system and for monitoring their effects on court operations and legal outcomes. It creates a dedicated oversight body that will review AI applications in courts, ensure transparency, and recommend safeguards to protect fairness, accuracy, and privacy in the justice system.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The bill requires the government to produce a report detailing how artificial intelligence is used to access unminimized information gathered under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It also includes additional provisions related to AI oversight and other related issues.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This bill would require a report on how artificial intelligence is used to access unminimized intelligence data collected under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, ensuring oversight and accountability. It also includes additional provisions related to the use of AI in national security contexts.

title: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This Act aims to reduce the United States’ dependence on Chinese artificial‑intelligence technology by limiting the use of Chinese AI hardware and software in federal projects. It also seeks to strengthen domestic AI research and secure supply chains to protect national security.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 is a law designed to stop companies from using AI algorithms to secretly cooperate in ways that harm competition. It sets rules and penalties to detect, deter, and punish such algorithmic collusion, helping to protect consumers and maintain a fair market.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act is a proposed law aimed at broadening the range of voices and perspectives represented in artificial intelligence systems. It seeks to make AI technology more inclusive and fair by ensuring diverse viewpoints are reflected in its design and deployment.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a federal law that establishes standards for how artificial intelligence systems can be developed, used, and monitored. It includes rules for transparency, safety, accountability, and consumer protection to balance innovation with the mitigation of potential risks.

title: LEARN AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
summary: The LEARN AI Act is a proposed law that aims to establish standards and best practices for the development and use of artificial intelligence technologies. It emphasizes transparency, accountability, and the protection of privacy and human rights while encouraging responsible innovation.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is a proposed law that protects the privacy of minors who interact with AI technologies. It requires companies to obtain parental consent before collecting or using a young person’s personal data, and imposes strict limits on how that data can be stored, shared, or used.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed law aimed at integrating artificial‑intelligence education into public schools across the United States. It would establish standards and provide resources for teachers and students to learn about AI technology, its applications, and ethical considerations.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 33 - 0.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2025 is a law that aims to strengthen AI learning opportunities across the United States by investing in educational programs at all levels. It allocates funding for research, teacher training, and curriculum development so that students and educators can stay up-to-date with AI technologies.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 establishes legal measures to prevent the unauthorized copying and distribution of AI models developed in the United States. It sets out penalties for violations and provides guidelines for ownership, licensing, and enforcement to protect AI intellectual property.
